newsitem.title: USA: Apogee ends long-term care operations, consolidates centers.
newsitem.headline: Apogee ends long-term care operations, consolidates centers.

text.p: Apogee Inc., a major provider of outpatient mental health services, said Tuesday it was ending its long-term care operations and consolidating several group practice centres in certain markets.

The company, based in King of Prussia, Pa., said it expects to complete most of the restructuring by the end of April 1997. It said it took a one-time charge of $14.1 million in the fourth quarter of 1996 for the actions.

Apogee made the announcement as it posted a net loss of $14.8 million, or $1.49 a share, in the fourth quarter ended Dec. 31. It lost $6.5 million, or 67 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues rose to $19.4 million from $18.0 million.

Lawrence Davies, president and chief operating officer, said the company has completed the first phase of its stabilisation of operations, eliminating parts of its business that had minimal profits but presented high risk.

He said Apogee was also in the process of closing, downsizing or consolidating 18 group practice centres whose performance has not met expectations, and is eliminating redundant centres in markets where the company has multiple locations.
The company has also eliminated over $1 million of corporate, regional and clinical overhead, he said.

Apogee said it has either closed, downsized or consolidated centres in the mid-Atlantic states, Arizona, Southern California, Illinois, southern Florida and Wisconsin to eliminate underperforming operations, overcapacity or redundancy.
It said it also has withdrawn from the outpatient group practice sector in Nashville, Tenn.; Ft. Walton Beach, Fla.; and Rhode Island markets.

Apogee, which operates 115 behavioural health centres in 13 states and Washington, D.C., said it has renegotiated its bank credit facility. It said that the facility, plus anticipated cash flows from operations, should be sufficient to meet the company's projected cash requirements in the coming year.
Apogee's stock fell 25 cents to $3.75 on Nasdaq at midday.
